turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The highest-efficiency MAPbI3 n-i-p cells in the training set share a small number of physically well-motivated features: a compact, selective electron contact (TiO2-c, SnO2 or C60/PCBM) that also passivates the perovskite interface, a high-mobility hole-selective contact whose HOMO is well aligned with the perovskite valence band (Spiro-MeOTAD, PTAA or a closely related triarylamine polymer), an inert high-work-function back contact (Au or MoO3/Au), a rigid glass/TCO substrate, and an absorber process that yields compact, low-defect films (spin-coating or co-evaporation).

c005 reproduces the second-highest training recipe almost exactly (TiO2-c/PCBM bilayer + PCDTBT polymer HTL + MoO3/Au). PCBM both improves electron extraction and strongly suppresses interfacial recombination; the polymer HOMO alignment and the MoO3 buffer are equally favourable. Its two-step spin process matches the 19.35 % cell, so film quality is expected to be comparable.

c064 uses the precise TiO2-c/SnO2-np electron-contact stack that produced the 20.85 % champion. SnO2 supplies higher mobility and a slightly deeper conduction band than TiO2 while the compact TiO2 under-layer guarantees hole-blocking; Spiro-MeOTAD/Au remains the classic high-selectivity hole contact. Even with a simpler spin-only absorber step the electronic structure is optimal.

c068 pairs the best low-temperature ETL (SnO2-np) with PTAA, the HTL that already reached 18.2 % in training. PTAA offers comparable (sometimes superior) hole selectivity and a more hydrophobic surface that improves perovskite morphology; the MoO3/Au contact further reduces series resistance.

c017 is a near-copy of the 17.9 % co-evaporated cell. Vacuum deposition yields high-purity, pin-hole-free films and atomically abrupt interfaces; C60 is an excellent electron acceptor and the F6-TCNNQ-doped TaTm layer supplies high hole conductivity while remaining electron-blocking.

c080 places a C60-containing interlayer on compact TiO2, a motif that already delivered 17.2 % with Spiro/Au. The fullerene passivates residual TiO2 traps and improves band alignment, while the rest of the stack is the standard high-performance n-i-p combination.

All other pool entries introduce at least one clear penalty (flexible substrate, missing compact layer, non-selective contact, carbon electrode, or an unproven/misaligned HTL) and are therefore ranked lower.

Final: c005, c064, c068, c017, c080
